MRCT regional consistency: simulations

The data-generating mechanism, the analytic layer and the campaign behind the case study

ForestSearch Package

2026-11-16

Source: vignettes/articles/mrct-consistency-simulations.qmd

Installing forestsearch

This article needs forestsearch 0.5.0 or later. Run the steps in a fresh R session.

# 1. a reliable CRAN mirror
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# 2. forestsearch from CRAN, which also installs every package it needs
install.packages("forestsearch")

# 3. two packages forestsearch only suggests, which this article uses (speff2trial for the
#    ACTG 175 data, latentcor for the copula expansion), and knitr for the tables
install.packages(c("speff2trial", "latentcor", "knitr"))

packageVersion("forestsearch")   # this article needs 0.5.0 or later

If a step asks whether to install packages from sources, answer no. The chunk below stops with a message naming anything that is missing, before any computation starts.

Installing from GitHub. The GitHub repository holds the version under development, which can be ahead of the CRAN release. Use it if you want changes that have not reached CRAN yet, or if the chunk below reports that your installed version is too old and CRAN has nothing newer. Do steps 1 to 3 first, so that every package forestsearch needs is already installed, then:

install.packages("remotes")
options(timeout = 600)   # R's default download limit of 60 seconds is too short for this repository
remotes::install_github("larry-leon/forestsearch", upgrade = "never")
packageVersion("forestsearch")

upgrade = "never" leaves the packages already installed as they are. The call downloads the whole forestsearch repository, several gigabytes, and builds only the package from it, so it takes several minutes. Restart R afterwards, so that the new version is the one loaded.

Code
needed <- c("inject_mrct_structure", "scale_dgm_hazard", "ahr_population", "ahr_limit", "ahr_design", "ahr_solve",
            "mrct_region_sims", "mrct_select_case", "mrct_case_study", "analysis_covariates", "get_dfpred",
            "mr_estimates_table", "mrct_record", "mrct_build_dgm", "mrct_trial_analysis", "mrct_core_summary",
            "ahr_truths_table", "ahr_design_table")
missing_fns <- setdiff(needed, getNamespaceExports("forestsearch"))
if (length(missing_fns))
  stop("This article needs forestsearch 0.5.0 or later (see 'Installing forestsearch'); ",
       "the installed version (", as.character(packageVersion("forestsearch")), ") lacks: ",
       paste(missing_fns, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
missing_pkgs <- c("speff2trial", "latentcor", "knitr")[!vapply(c("speff2trial", "latentcor", "knitr"), requireNamespace, NA, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs))
  stop("This article needs: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "),
       " (install.packages(c(", paste0('"', missing_pkgs, '"', collapse = ", "), ")).", call. = FALSE)
c(forestsearch = as.character(packageVersion("forestsearch")))
forestsearch
     "0.5.0"

Rendering this article yourself

Rendering needs the Quarto command-line tools and about five minutes. The article’s records are installed with the package, so only the .qmd file itself is needed. Download it into a scratch folder and render it there:

dir.create("~/Downloads/scratch/mrct-article", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
download.file("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/larry-leon/forestsearch/master/vignettes/articles/mrct-consistency-simulations.qmd",
              "~/Downloads/scratch/mrct-article/mrct-consistency-simulations.qmd")
cd ~/Downloads/scratch/mrct-article && quarto render mrct-consistency-simulations.qmd

The rendered mrct-consistency-simulations.html is written beside the .qmd. Delete the scratch folder when done.

This article is the simulation side of the regional-consistency strategy: how the report’s data-generating mechanism and cells were built, the analytic layer that predicts the design’s behaviour before any simulation, the committed campaign’s results, and how the case study of the application article (mrct-consistency) was found. It executes independently of that article: the case study’s objects, which the checks below compare against, are recomputed first (Section 1).

1 The case study’s objects, recomputed

The application article analyses one trial, replicate 5 of S2, from its shipped data (rep5_trial.csv) to its multiplier-resampling bounds, with every call explained. The simulation sections below check themselves against that analysis — the redraw of Section 3.4 must reproduce the trial, its Ĥ\hat H and its four Cox fits, and Section 3.5 reads its MR values — so this chunk recomputes the same objects by the one call of mrct_trial_analysis(), on the same arguments; the application article is the walkthrough.

Code
trial <- mrct_record("rep5_trial.csv")
covs <- c("z_age", "z_wtkg", "z_karnof", "z_preanti", "z_cd40", "z_cd80",
          "z_hemo", "z_homo", "z_drugs", "z_race", "z_gender", "z_symptom")
# the replicate's call seed, from the MR campaign's record of this trial
seed_rep5 <- mrct_record("mr_field_S2_rep5.csv")$seed
stopifnot(length(seed_rep5) == 1, !anyDuplicated(trial$id),
          all(c("id", "y_sim", "event_sim", "treat_sim", "z_region", covs, "flag_harm") %in% names(trial)))
stopifnot(RNGkind()[1] == "Mersenne-Twister")
t_mr <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
ta5 <- mrct_trial_analysis(
  trial, "y_sim", "event_sim", "treat_sim", region.name = "z_region", id.name = "id",
  truth.name = "flag_harm",
  fs_args = list(confounders.name = covs, conf_force = character(0),
                 conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                 use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE, maxk = 2,
                 hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
                 sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", effect_neighborhood = 0.20),
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", include_complement = TRUE, field_complement = TRUE,
                           draws = 2000, multiplier = "poisson", return_reselection = TRUE,
                           seed = seed_rep5))
t_mr <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_mr
four <- ta5$sets
itt_ub <- four$hi[four$set == "itt_all"]
stopifnot(itt_ub < 1)
reg <- trial$z_region == 1
trigger <- ta5$trigger
stopifnot(trigger)
fs <- ta5$fs
mr <- ta5$mr
Hhat_def <- ta5$Hhat
stopifnot(!is.null(fs$sg.harm), mr$ci_method == "field", mr$settings$draws == 2000,
          mr$field$n_out_used == mr$field$R_out)
in_Hhat <- ta5$in_Hhat
stopifnot(identical(in_Hhat, trial$id %in% c(fs$df.est$id[fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0],
                                              fs$df.test$id[fs$df.test$treat.recommend == 0])))
Hstar <- trial$flag_harm == 1                       # simulation only: H* is unknown in a real trial
set_label <- c(itt_all = "All patients, ITT", itt_region = "Region, ITT",
               region_Gstar = "Region minus H* (G*)", region_Ghat = "Region minus Ĥ (Ĝ)")
mr_tab <- mr_estimates_table(fs, est.scale = "hr", digits = 3)
mv <- attr(mr_tab, "mr_values")
cc <- mr$complement; fl <- mr$field
stopifnot(near(mv$naive_est, c(mr$naive$est, cc$naive$est), 1e-12),
          near(mv$field_bound, c(fl$lower_1s, fl$complement$upper_1s), 1e-12),
          near(mv$bonferroni_bound, c(fl$joint$bonf_lower_H, fl$joint$bonf_upper_Hc), 1e-12))
c(patients = nrow(trial), seconds_mr = round(t_mr, 1)); Hhat_def
  patients seconds_mr
    1000.0       53.4

Ĥ\hat H is {z_cd40 <= 236} & !{z_preanti <= 196}; the four sets and the bounds are read and discussed in the application article.

2 Setting up simulations from your own trial

This section treats rep5_trial.csv as if it were your trial, with its region observed: the column z_region is taken as recorded, and nothing about who is in the region is modelled. H*H^* and the effects in the cells are then your statements. Five steps, in order.

1. A data-generating mechanism that carries the observed region. inject_mrct_structure(), the function of the report’s build (Section 3.1), is given the trial and region = list(observed = "region"): with region$observed, the region is carried through the expansion with the covariates and nothing about membership is modelled. With loghr left at NULL the region’s prognostic log hazard ratio is estimated by the Weibull AFT fit, as the other covariates’ effects are; H*H^*, bb and hh are set as in the report’s build (spline_spec gives bb everywhere, x3 defines H*H^* = CD4 ≤\le 230 and multiplies the hazard ratio in it by h/bh/b), and the super-population is expanded by the copula. There is no scale_dgm_hazard() call here: replicate 5’s outcomes were drawn with every hazard already multiplied by 3, so the Weibull fit to them estimates the scaled intercept directly, and a scale_dgm_hazard(…, m = 3) call would multiply every hazard by 3 a second time.

Code
own <- mrct_record("rep5_trial.csv")
own <- own[, setdiff(names(own), c("id", "flag_harm"))]   # your trial has no flag_harm
names(own) <- sub("^z_", "", names(own))                   # plain names; the build adds z_
build_own <- function(h, b = 0.55, cut = 230) {
  mrct_build_dgm(
    own,
    outcome_var = "y_sim", event_var = "event_sim", treatment_var = "treat_sim",
    continuous_vars = c("age", "wtkg", "karnof", "preanti", "cd40", "cd80"),
    factor_vars = c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
    x_pred = "cd40",
    spline_spec = list(knot = 300, zeta = 800, log_hrs = rep(log(b), 3)),      # b
    region = list(observed = "region"),                                        # r estimated
    x3 = list(vars = "cd40", cuts = list(cd40 = cut), loghr = log(h / b)),     # h in H*
    n_super = 20000, expand = "copula", seed = 7L,
    continuous_vars_cens = c("age", "cd40"), factor_vars_cens = "symptom")
}
t_own <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
dgm_own <- build_own(h = 2)
t_own <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_own
for (w in attr(dgm_own, "build_warnings")) warning(w, call. = FALSE)   # kept by the build, shown here
Warning: Ran out of iterations and did not converge
Warning: Ran out of iterations and did not converge
Warning: Ran out of iterations and did not converge
Code
ds_own <- dgm_own$df_super
stopifnot(isTRUE(dgm_own$mrct$region$observed), dgm_own$mrct$region$z_name == "z_region",
          "z_cd40" %in% names(ds_own), !any(grepl("^z_z_", names(ds_own))),
          near(ds_own$loghr_po, ifelse(ds_own$z_cd40 <= 230, log(2), log(0.55)), 1e-12),
          all((ds_own$z_cd40 <= 230) == (ds_own$flag_harm == 1)))
r_own <- dgm_own$mrct$region$prognostic_loghr
c(rows = nrow(ds_own), region_super = mean(ds_own$z_region), region_trial = mean(own$region),
  Hstar = mean(ds_own$flag_harm), region_prognostic_loghr = r_own, generating_r = -log(4),
  build_warnings = length(attr(dgm_own, "build_warnings")), seconds = round(t_own, 1))
                   rows            region_super            region_trial
           20000.000000                0.195550                0.194000
                  Hstar region_prognostic_loghr            generating_r
               0.164250               -1.541238               -1.386294
         build_warnings                 seconds
               3.000000                0.500000

Every patient’s log hazard ratio is log⁡0.55\log 0.55 outside H*H^* and log⁡2\log 2 inside it. The region’s prognostic log hazard ratio, estimated from the trial, is r̂\hat r = -1.541 (er̂e^{\hat r} = 0.214); the mechanism that generated replicate 5 used r=−log⁡4r = -\log 4 = -1.386 (Section 3.1). The region is 19.6% of the super-population and 19.4% of the trial. The build took 0.5 seconds. Its 3 warnings, shown above, come from the censoring model’s fit: every censoring time in this trial lies between 29.01 and 39.98 months, that is, all censoring is administrative, and the Weibull fit to it does not converge. Trials are drawn below with cens_adjust = 50, which pushes that model far beyond the window, so all censoring is again administrative.

2. H*H^* and the cells. The build above is one cell: S2’s h=2h = 2 in H*H^* = CD4 ≤\le 230 and b=0.55b = 0.55 outside it. The other cells change only hh (shown, not run):

Code
h_cells <- c(N0 = 0.55, N1 = 0.75, S1 = 1, S2 = 2, S3 = 3, S4 = 4)   # h in H*; b = 0.55 outside
dgms_own <- lapply(h_cells, build_own)

Choosing the cells

A cell is one data-generating mechanism: your trial’s build with a stated H*H^*, a hazard ratio hh inside it and bb outside it, in every region. Choose hh as the sizes of harm you want the strategy to be able to explain, and keep cells in which there is nothing harmful to find (h=bh = b; hh between bb and 1; h=1h = 1): those are where the strategy explains a trigger that has no trial-wide explanation, and the rate at which it does so is a result to report.

3. The analytic layer on that mechanism. The four truths of the region, the non-region patients and G*G^*, and the design probabilities at n=1,000n = 1{,}000, with this trial’s analysis at 40 months and entry over 11.

Code
pop_own <- ahr_population(dgm_own, analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
sets_own <- c(region = "region", nonregion = "non-region", region_Gstar = "G* (region minus H*)")
lim_own <- ahr_truths_table(pop_own, sets = names(sets_own), b = 0.55, h = 2)
p_own <- ahr_design_table(pop_own, b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)
tab_own <- rbind(
  data.frame(row = unname(sets_own[lim_own$set]), a = f3(lim_own$marghr), b = f3(lim_own$marghr_inf),
             c = f3(lim_own$ahr), d = f3(lim_own$cde)),
  data.frame(row = c("P(trigger), n = 1,000", "P(oracle joint), n = 1,000"),
             a = f3(c(p_own[["p_trigger"]], p_own[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]])), b = "", c = "", d = ""))
knitr::kable(setNames(tab_own, c("", "margHR(40)", "margHR(∞)", "AHR", "CDE")), row.names = FALSE,
             align = "lrrrr", caption = "The analytic layer on the mechanism built from the trial (h = 2, b = 0.55).")

Code
# S2's values from the campaign's analytic record (the same numbers as in the analytic-layer section)
pred_S2 <- mrct_record("predictions_full.csv"); pred_S2 <- pred_S2[pred_S2$cell == "S2_rmlog4", ]
s2 <- function(q, set) { v <- pred_S2$value[pred_S2$quantity == q & pred_S2$set == set]; stopifnot(length(v) == 1); v }

As a reading, not a check: the region’s margHR(40) is 0.884 here against 0.868 in S2, P(trigger) 0.242 against 0.241 and the oracle joint 0.180 against 0.187 (Section 3.3); the build from one trial of 1,000 is not S2’s build from ACTG 175 and is not expected to reproduce it.

The analytic layer

ahr_population() on each cell’s mechanism, with your analysis time and entry period, then ahr_truths_table() on the sets you care about gives each set’s four truths: read margHR at the analysis time as the set’s windowed Cox limit, what its Cox estimate converges to — it moves with the event rate and the window while the AHR and CDE do not (the application article’s appendix shows why) — and the AHR and CDE as the effect in the set. ahr_design_table() at your trial size gives P(ITT ub < 1.0), P(region ITT > 1.0), P(trigger) and the oracle joint before any simulation; if P(trigger) is very small, the campaign will have few triggered trials to summarise. ahr_solve() places one free parameter so that P(trigger) reaches a target (Section 3.3.1). These are computed by quadrature and take seconds per cell.

4. The campaign. One mrct_region_sims() call per cell, with the identifier’s arguments of Section 1 (shown, not run; no campaign is run in this section):

Code
res_own <- mrct_region_sims(
  dgm_own, n_sims = 10000, n_sample = 1000, region_var = "z_region",
  sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", maxk = 2,
  hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  confounders.name = analysis_covariates(dgm_own, "observed"),   # all z_ but z_region
  conf_force = character(0),
  fs_args = list(conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                 effect_neighborhood = 0.20, use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE),
  sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50),
  analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
  parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 64, show_message = FALSE),
  details = FALSE, seed = 20261102, record = "full")

The campaign

Give mrct_region_sims() your cell’s mechanism, your trial size, your region variable and the identifier’s arguments you used in Section 1; sim_args and analysis_time carry the entry, window and dropout of the design. Keep record = "full": case selection reads the per-trial Cox fits it stores. Give each cell its own seed and record it: a replicate is redrawn from the mechanism, the call seed and its index. Before a full campaign, time a short run at the worker count you will use; the time per trial on a lightly loaded machine does not carry over to all workers busy.

5. Case selection and the summaries conditional on the trigger (shown, not run): the shares of the triggered trials, from the per-trial Cox fits of the full record, and a case chosen by the rule of Section 3.4.

Code
mrct_core_summary(res_own)                                    # the core rows, on the triggered trials
case_own <- mrct_select_case(res_own)                         # the first trial meeting the rule

Reading the results

Summarise the campaign conditional on the trigger: a team runs the joint analysis only when the trial is positive and the region’s estimate is above 1.0, so the triggered trials are the denominator that matters. Report for each cell the share of triggered trials with a declaration, the joint and, beside it, the oracle joint as the benchmark that removing H*H^* exactly would give under the stated mechanism (a benchmark, not a bound: in a given trial Ĝ\hat G can do better); then the same rows in the null cells. mrct_select_case() picks a case by a stated rule before it is looked at, and mrct_case_study() redraws and examines it (Section 3.4).

3 How replicate 5 was generated: the report’s simulation design

Replicate 5 is one trial drawn from the report’s S2 cell. This section is that design: the data-generating mechanism built from ACTG 175 (Section 3.1), the eight cells, the analytic layer (Section 3.3), and the rule and the calls by which replicate 5 was found and redrawn (Section 3.4); it closes with what can be said about replicate 5 only because it is simulated (Section 3.5).

3.1 The data-generating mechanism, built from ACTG 175

A Weibull accelerated-failure-time model is fitted to a published trial and expanded to a super-population of 20,000 rows by a Gaussian copula. A region of about 20% of patients is planted by a logistic model with odds ratio 3 on symptomatic status and no CD4 term, and its baseline hazard is shifted by rr; every patient’s hazard ratio is b=0.55b = 0.55 outside H*H^* = {CD4 ≤\le 230} and hh inside it, in every region; all hazards are then multiplied by m=3m = 3. Three calls build it, shown here as a reader would make them with their own trial.

1. The trial data. ACTG 175 (speff2trial), arms ZDV + ddI (arms == 1, experimental) and ddI alone (arms == 3, control). The outcome is days to the composite endpoint, in months, with event indicator cens; the prognostic covariates are age, weight (wtkg), Karnofsky score (karnof), days of prior antiretroviral therapy (preanti), baseline CD4 (cd40) and CD8 (cd80) counts, and the binary haemophilia (hemo), homosexual activity (homo), drug use (drugs), race, gender and symptomatic status (symptom).

Code
actg <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg$treat_mrct <- as.integer(actg$arms == 1L)   # ZDV + ddI = 1, ddI = 0
actg$time_months <- actg$days / 30.4375
rownames(actg) <- NULL
c(patients = nrow(actg), events = sum(actg$cens), experimental = sum(actg$treat_mrct))
    patients       events experimental
        1083          231          522

2. The region and the harmed subgroup. inject_mrct_structure() fits the Weibull model on the twelve covariates, expands it by the copula, plants the region (region: prevalence, the logistic model’s odds ratios, the prognostic log hazard ratio rr) and the harmed subgroup (spline_spec sets bb everywhere; x3 multiplies it by h/bh/b in CD4 ≤\le 230), here for cell S2 (h=2h = 2). The copula’s latent correlation is fitted live by latentcor (Suggests); without latentcor the call warns and uses the normal-score correlation instead, which gives a valid but different super-population.

Code
dgm_live <- inject_mrct_structure(
  actg,
  outcome_var = "time_months", event_var = "cens", treatment_var = "treat_mrct",
  continuous_vars = c("age", "wtkg", "karnof", "preanti", "cd40", "cd80"),
  factor_vars = c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
  x_pred = "cd40",
  spline_spec = list(knot = 300, zeta = 800, log_hrs = rep(log(0.55), 3)),  # b = 0.55
  region = list(prevalence = 0.20, or_pred = 1, x1_vars = "symptom", or_x1 = 3,
                loghr = -log(4),                                          # r
                band = list(cut = 230, or = 1)),
  x3 = list(vars = "cd40", cuts = list(cd40 = 230), loghr = log(2 / 0.55)),  # h = 2 in H*
  region_treat_loghr = NULL,
  n_super = 20000, expand = "copula", seed = 7L,
  continuous_vars_cens = c("age", "cd40"), factor_vars_cens = "symptom")

3. The hazard scale. scale_dgm_hazard() multiplies every hazard by mm on both arms, by shifting the fitted Weibull intercept (Section 5, the DGM in closed form), and leaves every hazard ratio unchanged. The Weibull fit to ACTG 175 carries that trial’s own event rate; m=3m = 3 raises it toward a modern trial’s (the application article gives both rates). The windowed Cox limits move with mm although no hazard ratio does; the application article’s appendix shows why.

Code
dgm_live <- scale_dgm_hazard(dgm_live, m = 3)
c(rows = nrow(dgm_live$df_super), region = mean(dgm_live$df_super$z_region),
  Hstar = mean(dgm_live$df_super$flag_harm))
     rows    region     Hstar
2.000e+04 2.006e-01 1.569e-01

To use your own trial, change these and nothing else:

  • the data frame and its outcome, event and treatment names (outcome_var, event_var, treatment_var; treatment coded 1 = experimental);
  • the covariates (continuous_vars, factor_vars, binary factors coded 0/1, and the censoring model’s continuous_vars_cens, factor_vars_cens);
  • the region model (region: its prevalence, the covariates that predict membership and their odds ratios, its prognostic log hazard ratio rr);
  • H*H^* and its effects: the covariate and cut that define it (x3, region$band), bb outside it (spline_spec$log_hrs) and hh inside it (x3$loghr =log⁡(h/b)= \log(h/b));
  • the analysis window and entry: the analysis time and the uniform entry period used below (analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11), and cens_adjust for the dropout model.

Reproducing this report’s build exactly

This chunk exists only so that the committed record is reproduced to the last digit on any platform: it builds the cells with the latent correlation stored with the campaign’s build (latent_R.csv, passed as latent_R), so no latentcor fit is made. A reader never needs it. Everything from the build check onward uses the cells built here (build_cell()).

Code
latent_R <- as.matrix(mrct_record("latent_R.csv", row.names = 1))

# One cell: hazard ratio h in H* = {CD4 <= 230}, b = 0.55 elsewhere, region
# prognostic log-HR r, all hazards x m; the calls of steps 2 and 3 above.
build_cell <- function(h, r = -log(4), b = 0.55, cut = 230, m = 3) {
  mrct_build_dgm(
    actg,
    outcome_var = "time_months", event_var = "cens", treatment_var = "treat_mrct",

Passed: the build equals the record (largest relative difference 4.3e-15). In this build the region holds 20.1% of the super-population, H*H^* holds 15.7% of all patients (16.5% of the region and 15.5% outside it), and at equal covariates a region patient has ere^{r} = 0.25 times the hazard of a non-region patient. The trial: n=1,000n = 1{,}000, 1:1, entry uniform over 11 months, analysis at 40 months; the Weibull dropout is pushed far beyond the window (cens_adjust = 50), so all censoring is administrative.

3.2 The cells

Six cells at r=−log⁡4r = -\log 4 differ only in the hazard ratio hh inside H*H^*; two later-enrolling cells keep S2’s effects and let the region enter later, with rr or the delay solved so that P(trigger) = 0.25 (Section 3.3.1). The specifications as the committed runs’ timing records state them:

3.3 The analytic layer in brief

For any patient set of such a DGM, analysed at a calendar time with uniform staggered entry and administrative censoring only, the analytic layer computes by quadrature (nothing is drawn) the exact limit of the two-sample Cox estimate on the set (the Struthers–Kalbfleisch root, margHR(40): the set’s windowed Cox limit), its information and robust variance, the expected events, the correlation between nested sets’ estimates, the set’s AHR and CDE, and the normal-approximation probability of the trigger at a trial size. ahr_population() reads the DGM; ahr_limit() gives a set’s four truths; ahr_design() gives the trial-level probabilities; ahr_solve() solves P(trigger) = target in one free parameter. ahr_truths_table() and ahr_design_table() tabulate ahr_limit() and ahr_design() over the cells. Section 5 states the formulas.

Code
t_an <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
cells6 <- cells[cells$delay == 0, ]
dgms <- lapply(setNames(cells6$h, cells6$cell), function(h) if (h == 2) dgm_S2 else build_cell(h = h))
pops <- lapply(dgms, ahr_population, analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
sets4 <- c(all = "all patients", nonregion = "non-region", region = "region", region_Gstar = "G* (region minus H*)")
h6 <- setNames(cells6$h, cells6$cell)
truths <- ahr_truths_table(pops, sets = names(sets4), b = 0.55, h = h6)
truths$horizon <- NULL; names(truths)[names(truths) == "marghr"] <- "marghr_40"
# against the committed predictions (the analytic records of the campaign)
pred <- rbind(mrct_record("predictions_full.csv"), mrct_record("predictions_S1.csv"))
pv <- function(cell, q, set) { v <- pred$value[pred$cell == cell & pred$quantity == q & pred$set == set]; stopifnot(length(v) == 1); v }
tr_ref <- mapply(function(c, s, q) pv(paste0(c, "_rmlog4"), q, s),
                 rep(truths$cell, 4), rep(truths$set, 4),
                 rep(c("marghr_40", "marghr_inf", "ahr", "cde"), each = nrow(truths)))
stopifnot(near(unlist(truths[c("marghr_40", "marghr_inf", "ahr", "cde")]), tr_ref))
tt <- truths
tt$set <- sets4[tt$set]; tt[3:6] <- lapply(tt[3:6], f3)
reg_S2 <- truths[truths$cell == "S2" & truths$set == "region", ]
stopifnot(reg_S2$marghr_40 < 1, reg_S2$cde > 1)

The four truths differ, and the difference is the point. The AHR and the CDE depend on a set only through its H*H^* shares; the two marginal ratios are bounded in hh and depend on the window and the prognostic structure. In S2 the region’s margHR(40) is 0.868, below 1, although its CDE is 1.097: the trigger in S2 is a sampling event around a regional limit below 1.

3.3.1 How r=−log⁡4r = -\log 4 was chosen, and the later-enrolling regions

The campaign’s regional shift was chosen to make the trigger frequent at the design: with S2’s effects (h=2h = 2), rr solving P(trigger) = 0.25 at n=1,000n = 1{,}000 is found by ahr_solve(), and the campaign rounded it to −log⁡4-\log 4. Each evaluation rebuilds the DGM at that rr.

Code
p_trig_r <- function(r, delay = NULL) {
  d <- build_cell(h = 2, r = r)
  ahr_design(ahr_population(d, 40, 11, entry_delay = delay), b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)$prob[["p_trigger"]]
}
roots <- mrct_record("entry_roots.csv")
rref <- function(tag) { x <- roots[startsWith(roots$row, tag), ]; stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1); x }
sol_r <- ahr_solve(p_trig_r, 0.25, c(-log(5), -log(3.5)), n_scan = 5L, tol = 1e-10)
ref0 <- rref("Reference: a = 0, r solving")
stopifnot(sol_r$n_roots == 1, abs(sol_r$roots - ref0$r) < 1e-6)
c(root_r = sol_r$roots, k_in_minus_log_k = exp(-sol_r$roots), committed_root = ref0$r,
  P_trigger_at_root = sol_r$values)
           root_r  k_in_minus_log_k    committed_root P_trigger_at_root
        -1.441190          4.225721         -1.441190          0.250000

The root is r=−log⁡4.226r = -\log 4.226, the committed -1.4412; the campaign used r=−log⁡4r = -\log 4, where P(trigger) is 0.241. The same target defines the two later-enrolling cells, in which the region’s patients enter aa months after the others (entry_delay): D1 keeps r=−log⁡2r = -\log 2 and solves the delay aa; D2 fixes a=6a = 6 months and solves rr.

Code
dgm_r2 <- build_cell(h = 2, r = -log(2))
p_trig_a <- function(a) ahr_design(ahr_population(dgm_r2, 40, 11, entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = a)),
                                   b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)$prob[["p_trigger"]]
sol_a <- ahr_solve(p_trig_a, 0.25, c(11, 12), scan = c(11, 12), tol = 1e-8)
sol_r6 <- ahr_solve(p_trig_r, 0.25, c(-log(3.5), -log(2.5)), n_scan = 5L, tol = 1e-10,
                    delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = 6))
d1r <- rref("D1:"); d2r <- rref("D2:")
stopifnot(sol_a$n_roots == 1, abs(sol_a$roots - d1r$a) < 1e-6,
          sol_r6$n_roots == 1, abs(sol_r6$roots - d2r$r) < 1e-6)
# the design layer at the two roots, against the committed root records
dD <- lapply(list(S2_D1 = list(r = -log(2), a = sol_a$roots), S2_D2 = list(r = sol_r6$roots, a = 6)), function(x) {
  d <- if (abs(x$r + log(2)) < 1e-12) dgm_r2 else build_cell(h = 2, r = x$r)
  ahr_design(ahr_population(d, 40, 11, entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = x$a)), 0.55, 2, 1000)
})
for (k in names(dD)) {
  x <- if (k == "S2_D1") d1r else d2r; p <- dD[[k]]$prob
  stopifnot(abs(p[["p_itt_ub_lt1"]] - x$p_itt_ub_lt1) < 1e-6, abs(p[["p_region_itt_gt1"]] - x$p_region_itt_gt1) < 1e-6,
            abs(p[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]] - x$p_trigger_Gstar_lt1) < 1e-6)
}

Code
t_an <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_an

A later-enrolling region is followed for less time, which keeps its 40-month window in the phase where the treated H*H^* patients are failing: a delay of 11.62 months at r=−log⁡2r = -\log 2, or of 6 months at r=−log⁡2.946r = -\log 2.946, does what the shift to −log⁡4-\log 4 does at no delay. The analytic computations of this section took 25 seconds.

3.4 Finding a case study

The report’s case example is one trial of the S2 cell, chosen by a stated rule: the first replicate, by index, that reaches the trigger, declares Ĥ\hat H and has region(Ĝ\hat G) < 1.0. Four calls find and examine such a trial in any simulation. They are shown on S2 with the campaign’s arguments and call seed at 100 replicates (nsims_demo, set at the top of the file), on workers from parallel::detectCores(); with the campaign’s seed these replicates are the campaign’s first 100. The same run is summarised beside the campaign in Section 4.6.

1. Simulate with the full record. mrct_region_sims(record = "full") keeps, for every trial, the Cox fits of the patient sets (the "estimators" attribute) that the selection reads.

Code
seed_S2 <- cells$seed[cells$cell == "S2"]
confounders <- analysis_covariates(dgm_S2, "observed")
workers_demo <- max(1L, min(parallel::detectCores(), nsims_demo))
t_demo <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
demo <- mrct_region_sims(
  dgm_S2, n_sims = nsims_demo, n_sample = 1000, region_var = "z_region",
  sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", maxk = 2,
  hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  confounders.name = confounders, conf_force = character(0),
  fs_args = list(conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                 effect_neighborhood = 0.20, use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE),
  sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50),
  analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
  parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = workers_demo, show_message = FALSE),
  details = FALSE, verbose_n_sims = 0, seed = seed_S2, record = "full")

3. Redraw it, and check it against Section 1. mrct_case_study() redraws trial k exactly as the simulation drew it (under L’Ecuyer-CMRG, by simulate_from_dgm() with seed equal to the call seed plus kk, restoring R’s default generator after), runs the identifier on its non-region patients with the simulation’s arguments (the arguments mrct_region_sims() takes directly go into fs_args here) and analyses the four sets. It runs here with mr_inference = FALSE: the MR draws are made once, in Section 1. The redrawn trial must equal the shipped rep5_trial.csv in every shipped column, to floating-point precision (see the note below the check), and its Ĥ\hat H and four sets those of Section 1; the article stops otherwise.

Code

                 conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),

  sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50),
  analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
  mr_inference = FALSE)
t_cs <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_cs

Passed: the redrawn trial equals rep5_trial.csv (largest relative difference 4.8e-15), and its Ĥ\hat H and four hazard ratios (largest absolute difference 0) are those of Section 1. The call took 8 seconds.

Platform precision

rep5_trial.csv was written on the Linux machine that ran the campaign. On another platform the redraw is the same trial, but continuous columns can differ in their last digits, because the linear-algebra library and floating-point arithmetic differ. On macOS (arm64, R 4.5.2, Apple’s Accelerate library), two columns differ, y_sim and z_wtkg, by at most 5e-15 relative, and every integer and 0/1 column is identical. The check therefore compares with a relative tolerance of 1e-12, not exactly.

3.5 Because this trial is simulated

With a real trial none of this is available: H*H^* is unknown, so there is no G*G^*, no oracle and no sensitivity or specificity. This subsection uses the S2 build and the analytic layer, so it is placed here, after them, rather than in the application article.

3.5.1 Ĥ\hat H against H*H^*, in the region and outside

Code
cc2 <- function(w) c(TP = sum(in_Hhat[w] & Hstar[w]), FP = sum(in_Hhat[w] & !Hstar[w]),
                     FN = sum(!in_Hhat[w] & Hstar[w]), TN = sum(!in_Hhat[w] & !Hstar[w]))
cf_non <- cc2(!reg); cf_reg <- cc2(reg)
stopifnot(identical(cf_non, cs$confusion$nonregion), identical(cf_reg, cs$confusion$region))
sens <- function(x) x[["TP"]] / (x[["TP"]] + x[["FN"]]); spec <- function(x) x[["TN"]] / (x[["TN"]] + x[["FP"]])
knitr::kable(data.frame(population = c("non-region (where the identifier ran)", "region (where Ĥ is applied)"),
                        n = c(sum(!reg), sum(reg)),

Code
hr4 <- setNames(four$hr, four$set)
stopifnot(hr4[["region_Gstar"]] < hr4[["region_Ghat"]], hr4[["region_Ghat"]] < 1, hr4[["itt_region"]] > 1)

Ĥ\hat H has the right variable and nearly the right cut, narrowed by prior therapy: it finds about half of the harmed patients (Sens 0.500 outside the region) and almost no one else (Spec 0.988). Applied in the region it removes 20 patients, 18 of them in H*H^*, and region(Ĝ\hat G) is 0.844, between the whole region and the oracle region(G*G^*) = 0.736, as a partial removal of H*H^* should.

3.5.3 The four sets beside their limits

The analytic layer’s limit of each set’s Cox estimate, with the set’s AHR and CDE; Ĝ\hat G is replicate 5’s rule applied to every super-population row of the region. zz is the estimate’s distance from its limit in units of the robust SE that the limit implies at the set’s size.

Code
Hhat_super <- get_dfpred(dgm_S2$df_super, sg.harm = fs$sg.harm, version = 2)$treat.recommend == 0
lim_sets <- list(itt_all = "all", itt_region = "region", region_Gstar = "region_Gstar",
                 region_Ghat = pop_S2$region & !Hhat_super)
lims <- lapply(lim_sets, function(s) ahr_limit(pop_S2, s, b = 0.55, h = 2, variance = TRUE))
z <- (log(four$hr) - vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "beta")) /
  sqrt(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "var_robust") / four$n)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Set = set_label[four$set], `replicate 5 HR` = f3(four$hr),
  `margHR(40)` = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "hr")), `margHR(∞)` = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "marghr_inf")),
  AHR = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "ahr")), CDE = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "cde")),
  z = f2(z), check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrr",

The region’s limit, margHR(40) = 0.868, is below 1; replicate 5’s regional estimate sits 0.56 robust SDs above it. A regional prognostic effect, a harmed subgroup and a finite window move the region’s limit toward 1, and sampling did the rest.

4 Simulation results

The campaign ran 10,000 replicates per cell at n=1,000n = 1{,}000 with mrct_region_sims(). Its records are summarised here from the shipped core tables; Section 4.6 summarises the small run of Section 3.4 beside them.

4.1 The core operating characteristics at n=1,000n = 1{,}000

Every count-derived entry equals its recount from the numeric records. Reading: the trigger becomes more frequent as the harm in H*H^* grows (from 540 triggered trials in N0 to 3,048 in S4). Where there is something to find (S2–S4) a subgroup is declared in essentially every triggered trial, it overlaps H*H^* with sensitivity about 0.6 and specificity above 0.95, and the joint holds in 51.2% to 61.6% of triggered trials, against an oracle benchmark of 77.7% to 89.2%. Where there is nothing harmful to find (N0) a subgroup is still declared in 52.2% of triggered trials and the joint holds in 10.6%: the strategy “explains” some triggers when there is nothing to explain, which is why it is signal generation.

4.3 Predicted against observed

The analytic layer’s trigger probability and oracle joint (computed in Section 3.3) against the campaign’s frequencies over 10,000 trials, with zz the difference in binomial SEs.

Code
po <- rbind(
  data.frame(cell = d1000$cell, pred_trigger = d1000$p_A_B, pred_oracle = d1000$p_A_B_Cstar,
             obs_trigger = cn$n_trigger[match(paste0(d1000$cell, "_rmlog4"), cn$setting)] / 10000,
             obs_oracle = cn$n_Gstar_lt1[match(paste0(d1000$cell, "_rmlog4"), cn$setting)] / 10000),
  data.frame(cell = names(dD), pred_trigger = vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_trigger"]], 0),
             pred_oracle = vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]], 0),
             obs_trigger = vapply(names(dD), gv, 0, q = "p_trigger"),
             obs_oracle = vapply(names(dD), gv, 0, q = "p_trigger_Gstar_lt1")))

4.4 Post-selection inference on Ĥ\hat H in the triggered trials

The MR field call of Section 1 was run on every triggered trial of the eight cells. Three shares are read by location, against clinically meaningful hazard ratios: the share of declared triggered trials whose Ĥ\hat H lower bound is above 0.90 and above 1.0, and the share whose Ĥc\hat H^c upper bound is below 1.0.

mv_ <- function(row, k) mfc[[k]][mfc$row == row]

Reading: where there is nothing harmful to find (N0, N1, S1) the lower bound for Ĥ\hat H almost never excludes a hazard ratio of 0.90 (0.30% at most): the bound does not mistake a selected subgroup for a harmed one. With harm h=2h = 2 (S2) it excludes 0.90 in 18.70% of declared triggered trials and 1.0 in 13.60%; with h=4h = 4 in 88.90% and 83.90%. The upper bound for Ĥc\hat H^c is below 1.0 in every cell’s declared triggered trials (100.00% at least): the patients outside Ĥ\hat H benefit. The spread between the de-biased estimate and the bound is the price of the selection.

4.5 The campaign code and its wall-clock

The committed campaign, one mrct_region_sims() call per cell, with every argument (shown, not run):

Code
campaign_cell <- function(dgm, seed, n_sims = 10000L, workers = 64L, entry_delay = NULL) {
  mrct_region_sims(
    dgm, n_sims = n_sims, n_sample = 1000, region_var = "z_region",
    sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", maxk = 2,
    hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
    confounders.name = analysis_covariates(dgm, "observed"), conf_force = character(0),
    fs_args = list(conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                   effect_neighborhood = 0.20, use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE),
    sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50,
                    entry_delay = entry_delay),
    analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
    parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = workers, show_message = FALSE),
    details = FALSE, seed = seed, record = "full")
}
# the six cells at r = -log 4
for (k in c("N0", "N1", "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"))
  res[[k]] <- campaign_cell(build_cell(h = cells$h[cells$cell == k]), seed = cells$seed[cells$cell == k])
# the later-enrolling cells: the region enters a months later
res$S2_D1 <- campaign_cell(build_cell(h = 2, r = -log(2)), seed = cells$seed[cells$cell == "S2_D1"],
                           entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = sol_a$roots))
res$S2_D2 <- campaign_cell(build_cell(h = 2, r = sol_r6$roots), seed = cells$seed[cells$cell == "S2_D2"],
                           entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = 6))

The committed runs predate record = "full" and entry_delay: their per-replicate records were rebuilt by redrawing each trial from its seed, which record = "full" now returns directly from the same trials, and the later-enrolling cells stored a fixed entry time per super-population row (entry_var), where entry_delay redraws the entry each trial with the same law. The timing records:

5 Appendix: the analytic tools

This appendix condenses Section 3.5 of the accompanying manuscript (in submission) and its supporting document Analytic Derivations, where the derivations are; the sections of that document are cited inline below by their section numbers (the development record is in the theory notes AHR_mrct_dgm.qmd and AHR_complete.qmd and Chapter 6 of the technical report, in the mrct-consistency repository). Each display carries the manuscript’s role tag: [computed] results produce reported numbers and name the forestsearch function that computes them; [identity] results are exact consequences of them; [assumption] marks a modelling assumption; and [interpretation] marks an approximation used only to read the exact results, which enters no reported number. The modelling assumptions used below are (A1) 1:1 allocation, (A3) uniform staggered entry with a calendar-time analysis, entry independent of event time, and (A5) joint asymptotic normality; the full list (A1)–(A6) is in the Analytic Derivations, §B.1.3.

The DGM in closed form. The Weibull AFT draws log⁡T=μ+ℓz(x)+τε\log T = \mu + \ell_z(x) + \tau\varepsilon with ε=log⁡Exp(1)\varepsilon = \log \mathrm{Exp}(1), so F‾(s∣x,z)=exp⁡{−Λ0(s)eθz(x)},Λ0(s)=(se−μ)1/τ,θz(x)=−ℓz(x)/τ, \bar F(s \mid x, z) = \exp\{-\Lambda_0(s)\, e^{\theta_z(x)}\}, \qquad \Lambda_0(s) = (s e^{-\mu})^{1/\tau}, \qquad \theta_z(x) = -\ell_z(x)/\tau , a proportional-hazards model in (x,z)(x, z) with Weibull baseline. The prognostic part is θ0(x)=x⊤β+r𝟏{x∈R}\theta_0(x) = x^\top\beta + r\,\mathbf 1\{x \in R\}, the treatment effect ψ(x)=θ1(x)−θ0(x)=log⁡b+log⁡(h/b)𝟏{CD4≤230}\psi(x) = \theta_1(x) - \theta_0(x) = \log b + \log(h/b)\,\mathbf 1\{\mathrm{CD4} \le 230\}, and scale_dgm_hazard() sets μ←μfit−τlog⁡m\mu \leftarrow \mu_{\text{fit}} - \tau \log m, multiplying every hazard by mm and leaving every θ\theta unchanged.

The clock and the arm functions. Each patient’s event time TT follows the Weibull proportional-hazards law above, with log hazard multiplier θz\theta_z on arm z∈{0,1}z \in \{0, 1\}. Λ0\Lambda_0 is continuous and strictly increasing from 0 to ∞\infty, so on the operational clock

[identity] u=Λ0(s)=(se−μ)1/τ,P(Λ0(T)>u)=P(T>Λ0−1(u))=e−ueθz u = \Lambda_0(s) = \bigl(s\,e^{-\mu}\bigr)^{1/\tau}, \qquad P\bigl(\Lambda_0(T) > u\bigr) = P\bigl(T > \Lambda_0^{-1}(u)\bigr) = e^{-u e^{\theta_z}} every patient is exponential with rate eθze^{\theta_z} (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3a). For a patient set 𝒮\mathcal S, the set-averaged arm survivor and event-density functions on the operational clock are therefore finite mixtures of exponentials,

[computed] ahr_limit() Az(u)=1|𝒮|∑i∈𝒮e−ueθz,i,fz(u)=−Az′(u)=1|𝒮|∑i∈𝒮eθz,ie−ueθz,i A_z(u) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal S|}\sum_{i \in \mathcal S} e^{-u e^{\theta_{z,i}}}, \qquad f_z(u) = -A_z'(u) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal S|}\sum_{i \in \mathcal S} e^{\theta_{z,i}} e^{-u e^{\theta_{z,i}}} (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3a), and arm zz of the set has marginal survivor function Az(Λ0(s))A_z(\Lambda_0(s)) in on-study time.

The window function. Entry EE is uniform on (0,te)(0, t_e) and independent of the event time, and the trial is analysed at calendar time tat_a (here 11 and 40 months). A patient is at risk at on-study time ss only if they entered by ta−st_a - s, which has probability H(ta−s)H(t_a - s) with H(v)=min⁡{1,max⁡(v,0)/te}H(v) = \min\{1, \max(v, 0)/t_e\}. Composing with the inverse clock Λ0−1(u)=eμuτ\Lambda_0^{-1}(u) = e^{\mu} u^{\tau} gives the probability Hw(u)H_w(u) that a patient is still inside their follow-up window at operational time uu:

[identity] Hw(u)=H(ta−Λ0−1(u))={1,0≤u≤uκ,ta−eμuτte,uκ<u<Λ0(ta),0,u≥Λ0(ta),uκ=Λ0(ta−te) H_w(u) = H\bigl(t_a - \Lambda_0^{-1}(u)\bigr) = \begin{cases} 1, & 0 \le u \le u_\kappa,\\[2pt] \dfrac{t_a - e^{\mu} u^{\tau}}{t_e}, & u_\kappa < u < \Lambda_0(t_a),\\[2pt] 0, & u \ge \Lambda_0(t_a), \end{cases} \qquad u_\kappa = \Lambda_0(t_a - t_e) (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3b). The entry kink uκu_\kappa is the last operational time at which every patient is still in their window; beyond it HwH_w falls, linearly in ss, and it is 0 from Λ0(ta)\Lambda_0(t_a) on.

The expected-event measure of the window. Per patient of 𝒮\mathcal S, the expected number of events at operational time uu inside the window is

[identity] dN(u)=12Hw(u){f1(u)+f0(u)}du,∫dN=12(D1+D0),Dz=∫Hwfzdu dN(u) = \tfrac12 H_w(u)\bigl\{f_1(u) + f_0(u)\bigr\}\,du, \qquad \int dN = \tfrac12\bigl(D_1 + D_0\bigr), \qquad D_z = \int H_w f_z\,du (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3a for dNdN, §B.5 for its total). A patient on arm zz has an event at uu with density fz(u)f_z(u), and the event falls in the window with probability Hw(u)H_w(u); the product HwfzH_w f_z is exact because entry and event time are independent (A3), and the 12\tfrac12 averages the two arms under 1:1 allocation (A1). DzD_z is arm zz’s per-patient probability of an event in the window, so ∫dN\int dN is the expected number of window events per patient of 𝒮\mathcal S. A trial of nn patients has n𝒮∼Bin(n,π𝒮)n_{\mathcal S} \sim \mathrm{Bin}(n, \pi_{\mathcal S}) of them in 𝒮\mathcal S and therefore expects nπ𝒮∫dNn\pi_{\mathcal S}\int dN window events from 𝒮\mathcal S: the expected-events number the layer reports (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.1.2 and §B.8.2).

The events-weighted average over the window. For a function gg of operational time,

[identity] ⟨g⟩N=∫gdN∫dN \langle g\rangle_N = \frac{\int g\,dN}{\int dN} is the average of gg over the expected events in the window (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.5). Every windowed summary of the layer is an integral or an average under dNdN: the score and information, the events form and the imbalance moments below.

The least-false limit. On a patient set 𝒮\mathcal S patient ii has window ta−Eit_a - E_i, at-risk process Yi(s)Y_i(s) and counting process Ni(s)N_i(s). The two-sample Cox estimate β̂𝒮\hat\beta_{\mathcal S} is the root of the partial-likelihood score Un,𝒮(β)=∑i∈𝒮∫0ta{Zi−Z‾𝒮(s,β)}dNi(s)U_{n,\mathcal S}(\beta) = \sum_{i \in \mathcal S}\int_0^{t_a}\{Z_i - \bar Z_{\mathcal S}(s, \beta)\}\,dN_i(s), Z‾𝒮=S𝒮(1)/S𝒮(0)\bar Z_{\mathcal S} = S^{(1)}_{\mathcal S}/S^{(0)}_{\mathcal S}. The model is misspecified (the set mixes patients with different hazard ratios), and β̂𝒮\hat\beta_{\mathcal S} converges to the least-false parameter β𝒮*\beta^*_{\mathcal S} (Struthers and Kalbfleisch 1986; Gerds and Schumacher 2001), which on the operational clock is the unique root of the population score

[computed] ahr_population(), ahr_limit() U𝒮(β)=12∫0Λ0(ta)Hw(u){f1(u)−r(u,β)[f1(u)+f0(u)]}du,r(u,β)=eβA1(u)eβA1(u)+A0(u), \begin{aligned} U_{\mathcal S}(\beta) &= \tfrac12 \int_0^{\Lambda_0(t_a)} H_w(u)\Bigl\{f_1(u) - r(u, \beta)\,\bigl[f_1(u) + f_0(u)\bigr]\Bigr\}\,du,\\ r(u, \beta) &= \frac{e^\beta A_1(u)}{e^\beta A_1(u) + A_0(u)} , \end{aligned} with margHR(40) =eβ𝒮*= e^{\beta^*_{\mathcal S}} at ta=40t_a = 40 (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3a and §B.3c). The root is unique because ∂U𝒮/∂β=−∫r(1−r)dN<0\partial U_{\mathcal S}/\partial\beta = -\int r(1 - r)\,dN < 0: the Struthers–Kalbfleisch limit written on the operational clock. With δ(u)=log⁡{A1/A0}\delta(u) = \log\{A_1/A_0\} and the set’s instantaneous hazard ratio ϑ𝒮(u)=(f1/A1)/(f0/A0)\vartheta_{\mathcal S}(u) = (f_1/A_1)/(f_0/A_0) the score is ∫{expit⁡(log⁡ϑ𝒮+δ)−expit⁡(β+δ)}dN\int\{\operatorname{expit}(\log\vartheta_{\mathcal S} + \delta) - \operatorname{expit}(\beta + \delta)\}\,dN: the score of a time-varying-effect model whose profile is induced by composition. ahr_limit() evaluates the arm functions as finite sums over the super-population rows of the set, integrates by composite Gauss–Legendre quadrature on geometric panels in uu with breaks at the entry kinks, and finds the root by uniroot(). Breslow’s estimator converges to Λ0*\Lambda_0^*, with λ0*/λ0=(f1+f0)/(eβ*A1+A0)\lambda_0^*/\lambda_0 = (f_1 + f_0)/(e^{\beta^*}A_1 + A_0) in operational time (Analytic Derivations).

margHR(∞\infty) is eβe^{\beta} at the root of the same score with no censoring, Hw≡1H_w \equiv 1 and the integral run to infinity,

[computed] ahr_limit() U𝒮∞(β)=12∫0∞{f1(u)−r(u,β)[f1(u)+f0(u)]}du U^{\infty}_{\mathcal S}(\beta) = \tfrac12 \int_0^{\infty} \Bigl\{f_1(u) - r(u, \beta)\,\bigl[f_1(u) + f_0(u)\bigr]\Bigr\}\,du (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3c); it depends on the set’s patients alone, not on μ\mu or τ\tau. With ψ=θ1−θ0\psi = \theta_1 - \theta_0 a patient’s log hazard ratio, p𝒮p_{\mathcal S} the set’s H*H^* patient share and ω𝒮0=∑𝒮∩H*eθ0/∑𝒮eθ0\omega^0_{\mathcal S} = \sum_{\mathcal S \cap H^*} e^{\theta_0} / \sum_{\mathcal S} e^{\theta_0} the share of its baseline hazard carried by H*H^*, the set’s other truths are closed forms:

[computed] ahr_limit() AHR(𝒮)=exp⁡{1|𝒮|∑𝒮ψ}=b1−p𝒮hp𝒮,CDE(𝒮)=∑𝒮eθ1∑𝒮eθ0=(1−ω𝒮0)b+ω𝒮0h \mathrm{AHR}(\mathcal S) = \exp\Bigl\{\tfrac1{|\mathcal S|}\textstyle\sum_{\mathcal S}\psi\Bigr\} = b^{1 - p_{\mathcal S}} h^{p_{\mathcal S}}, \qquad \mathrm{CDE}(\mathcal S) = \frac{\sum_{\mathcal S} e^{\theta_1}}{\sum_{\mathcal S} e^{\theta_0}} = (1 - \omega^0_{\mathcal S})\,b + \omega^0_{\mathcal S}\,h (derivation: Analytic Derivations, §B.3c).

The events form. With δ(u)=log⁡{A1(u)/A0(u)}\delta(u) = \log\{A_1(u)/A_0(u)\} the log ratio of the arms’ numbers at risk and P‾=D1/(D1+D0)\bar P = D_1/(D_1 + D_0), the score equation at the root reads exactly

[identity] P‾=D1D1+D0=⟨expit⁡(β𝒮*+δ)⟩N: \bar P = \frac{D_1}{D_1 + D_0} = \bigl\langle\operatorname{expit}\bigl(\beta^*_{\mathcal S} + \delta\bigr)\bigr\rangle_N : the experimental arm’s share of the expected window events equals the events-weighted average of the fitted risk-set share. Expanding the right side to second order about δ‾=⟨δ⟩N\bar\delta = \langle\delta\rangle_N, where the first-order term vanishes, gives

[interpretation] β𝒮*≈log⁡D1D0−δ‾−12(1−2P‾)VarN(δ),VarN(δ)=⟨δ2⟩N−δ‾2: \beta^*_{\mathcal S} \approx \log\frac{D_1}{D_0} - \bar\delta - \tfrac12(1 - 2\bar P)\,\mathrm{Var}_N(\delta), \qquad \mathrm{Var}_N(\delta) = \langle\delta^2\rangle_N - \bar\delta^{\,2} : the marginal hazard ratio is the ratio of the arms’ event probabilities divided by the geometric-mean ratio of the arms’ numbers at risk at the event times, corrected by the dispersion of that ratio. The approximation ladder, and its tabulation against the exact root, are in the Analytic Derivations, §B.6. Setting every imbalance to zero gives the first-order form

[interpretation] expit⁡(β𝒮*)≈(1−ω𝒮)b1+b+ω𝒮h1+h, \operatorname{expit}(\beta^*_{\mathcal S}) \approx (1 - \omega_{\mathcal S})\frac{b}{1+b} + \omega_{\mathcal S}\frac{h}{1+h}, ω𝒮\omega_{\mathcal S} the share of the set’s expected events in the window carried by H*H^*, with a closed form through the event probability π(θ)=1−1te∫ta−tetaexp⁡{−cw1/τ}dw\pi(\theta) = 1 - \tfrac{1}{t_e}\int_{t_a - t_e}^{t_a}\exp\{-c\,w^{1/\tau}\}\,dw, c=eθ−μ/τc = e^{\theta - \mu/\tau} (Analytic Derivations). It fails for a harmed H*H^*, whose treated patients are used up early.

The clock identity and the frailty reading. Under a uniform effect (h=bh = b), A1(u)=L𝒮(bu)A_1(u) = L_{\mathcal S}(bu) and A0(u)=L𝒮(u)A_0(u) = L_{\mathcal S}(u) with L𝒮L_{\mathcal S} the Laplace transform of eθ0e^{\theta_0} over the set: the covariate-driven baseline acts as a frailty, and ϑ𝒮(s)=bℓ𝒮(bΛ0(s))/ℓ𝒮(Λ0(s))\vartheta_{\mathcal S}(s) = b\,\ell_{\mathcal S}(b\Lambda_0(s))/\ell_{\mathcal S}(\Lambda_0(s)), with ℓ𝒮\ell_{\mathcal S} the survival-weighted mean of eθ0e^{\theta_0} among the set’s survivors, drifts from bb toward 1 as high-hazard patients leave. The regional prognostic shift rr adds rr to θ0\theta_0 on every region row, so for a set inside the region the arm functions at shift rr are those at shift 0 read at erue^r u:

[identity] Az(r)(u)=Az(0)(eru),fz(r)(u)=erfz(0)(eru). A^{(r)}_z(u) = A^{(0)}_z(e^r u), \qquad f^{(r)}_z(u) = e^r f^{(0)}_z(e^r u) . rr is a clock on the region: margHR(∞\infty), the AHR and the CDE do not depend on rr; only the windowed margHR(40) moves, and a region delayed by aa is the undelayed region analysed at horizon ta−at_a - a. The hazard multiplier is the same clock on every patient: multiplying every hazard by mm gives Az(m)(u)=Az(mu)A^{(m)}_z(u) = A_z(m u), so a trial at mm times the hazards, analysed at tat_a with entry over tet_e, is the unscaled trial analysed at mτtam^{\tau} t_a with entry over mτtem^{\tau} t_e; again only margHR(40) moves. With a harmed H*H^* the region’s profile starts at its CDE, above 1, while the treated H*H^* patients fail, crosses 1 once they are spent and falls toward bb, before drifting back up as high-hazard patients leave; the slower clock keeps the 40-month window in the harm phase and moves the region’s margHR(40) toward the null. A regional prognostic effect, a harmed subgroup and a finite window are needed together. The application article’s appendix draws this profile for S2, for all patients and for the region, and margHR(40) against mm.

The design layer. [assumption] (A5): the three estimates entering the trigger and the oracle joint, β̂all\hat\beta_{\text{all}}, β̂R\hat\beta_R and β̂G*\hat\beta_{G^*}, are treated as jointly normal around their limits, with the robust standard deviations and the correlations of their influences. For a trial of nn patients, 1:1, with n𝒮∼Bin(n,π𝒮)n_{\mathcal S} \sim \mathrm{Bin}(n, \pi_{\mathcal S}) in 𝒮\mathcal S and i1=∫r(1−r)dNi_1 = \int r(1 - r)\,dN the information per patient,

[computed] ahr_design() Var(β̂𝒮)≈1i1E[1n𝒮](model),≈Σi12E[1n𝒮](robust),E[1n𝒮]≈1nπ𝒮{1+1−π𝒮nπ𝒮}, \begin{aligned} \mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta_{\mathcal S}) &\approx \frac{1}{i_1}\,\mathrm E\Bigl[\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr] && \text{(model)},\\ &\approx \frac{\Sigma}{i_1^2}\,\mathrm E\Bigl[\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr] && \text{(robust)},\\ \mathrm E\Bigl[\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr] &\approx \frac{1}{n\pi_{\mathcal S}}\Bigl\{1 + \frac{1 - \pi_{\mathcal S}}{n\pi_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr\}, \end{aligned} Σ\Sigma the variance of the Lin–Wei influence (Analytic Derivations). Under a common proportional-hazards model the correlation of nested estimates is the square root of the information share, ρ=Corr(β̂all,β̂R)=IR/Iall\rho = \mathrm{Corr}(\hat\beta_{\text{all}}, \hat\beta_R) = \sqrt{I_R/I_{\text{all}}}; under misspecification the layer uses the exact covariance of the two influences. With μ𝒮=β𝒮*\mu_{\mathcal S} = \beta^*_{\mathcal S}, σ𝒮\sigma_{\mathcal S} the robust SD, σ̃all\tilde\sigma_{\text{all}} the model SE and z0.975=Φ−1(0.975)≈1.96z_{0.975} = \Phi^{-1}(0.975) \approx 1.96,

[computed] ahr_design() P(ITT ub<1)=Φ(zA),zA=−z0.975σ̃all−μallσall;P(region ITT>1)=Φ(−zB),zB=−μRσR;P(trigger)=Φ2(zA,−zB;−ρall,R), \begin{aligned} P(\text{ITT ub} < 1) &= \Phi(z_A), & z_A &= \frac{-z_{0.975}\,\tilde\sigma_{\text{all}} - \mu_{\text{all}}}{\sigma_{\text{all}}};\\ P(\text{region ITT} > 1) &= \Phi(-z_B), & z_B &= \frac{-\mu_R}{\sigma_R};\\ P(\text{trigger}) &= \Phi_2(z_A, -z_B; -\rho_{\text{all},R}), \end{aligned} and the oracle joint is the trivariate Φ3(zA,−zB,zC;𝑹)\Phi_3(z_A, -z_B, z_C; \mathbf R) with zC=−μG*/σG*z_C = -\mu_{G^*}/\sigma_{G^*}, 𝑹\mathbf R the correlation matrix of (β̂all,−β̂R,β̂G*)(\hat\beta_{\text{all}}, -\hat\beta_R, \hat\beta_{G^*}) (ahr_design(); derivation: Analytic Derivations).

Per-patient entry. With entry_delay, patient ii enters at ai+Ea_i + E, E∼U(0,te)E \sim U(0, t_e); each patient carries their own entry factor Hw,i(u)H_{w,i}(u), and the arm functions of the score become the entry-weighted sums AH(u)=|𝒮|−1∑𝒮Hw,i(u)e−ueθ1,iA_{H}(u) = |\mathcal S|^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal S} H_{w,i}(u)\,e^{-u e^{\theta_{1,i}}} (and likewise for the control arm and the event densities), with quadrature breaks at each entry group’s kinks. For a set inside a region delayed by aa, the limit equals the undelayed limit at horizon ta−at_a - a: a later-enrolling region is a region analysed earlier. With no delay every Hw,iH_{w,i} is the common HwH_w and the layer is the one above (derivation: Analytic Derivations).
